text:
maya: anyone else seeing a spike in small-pod evictions in ap-south1? ~120 evictions in the last 10m, mostly tiny gpu jobs getting preempted
sam: i see it — eviction rate up on scheduler.metrics.evictions_total for ap-south1, small-pod class. also latency on packing up 95th went from 120ms -> 450ms
deploy-bot: rollout gpu-labels-v2 (gitops) completed by olivia 5 minutes ago :white_check_mark:
noah: oh that rollout touched node labels `gpu-tier` and added `gpu-tier=v2` to new nodes. any chance scheduler lost affinity rules?
maya: eviction reason from kubelet logs: "PodPreempted: node has taint gpu-tier=v2:NoSchedule, pod lacks toleration"
olivia: ugh, i added the label to help new binpacking policies, but didn't add tolerations to the tiny-pod job template. my bad.
jordan: quick mitigation: revert label rollout or add toleration to the tiny-pod DaemonSet/PodSpec. which is faster?
sam: short-term revert on the node-labeling patch is fastest. but we should avoid a full revert if we can patch the scheduler policy or add a default toleration for small GPU workloads in the quota controller
maya: agreed. reverting labels on autoscaler-managed nodes might be noisy. can we cordon new nodes and reprovision?
noah: runbook idea: 1) patch the tiny-pod workload to tolerate `gpu-tier=v2` 2) scale-down and delete a few new nodes to force rejoin without the label 3) rollback label in gitops if patching not safe
olivia: i'll open a canary patch for the tiny-pod helm chart now. quick toleration: 
```yaml
tolerations:
  - key: "gpu-tier"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "v2"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```
noah: thanks. also we should check the packing heuristic — the new label changed topology spread constraints for some jobs, causing densification on a subset of racks and NVLINK hot spots, which increased thermal throttling and then preemptions cascaded
jordan: where can i see the rack-level packing skew? prometheus panel?
sam: dashboards: infra/gpu/pool-az-packing and infra/gpu/rack-heatmap. look at `gpu_alloc_fraction_by_rack` and `nvlink_thermal_trip_count` for ap-south1c
maya: i'm running: `kubectl get pods -n batch -o wide | grep Evicted` and tailing kubelet on a hotspot node — sharing tail output in #incidents if anyone wants it
olivia: can we do a non-invasive scheduler tweak: make small-pods prefer toleration rather than strict NoSchedule? i.e. change taint to NoExecute?
noah: NoExecute would kick existing pods off, risky. Better: add toleration w/ tolerationSeconds? small pods are short-lived, tolerate indefinitely is fine
jordan: cost note: this caused a weird autoscaler churn — several node groups trimmed then re-provisioned, bumped hourly instance spend. finance pinged about a cost blip
maya: action items: olivia will patch tiny-pod toleration (canary -> roll), sam will open gitops rollback PR for node-label rollout if patch misses, noah will watch packing/rack metrics and post a short summary in 15m, jordan will calculate cost delta and flag if >5% hourly
olivia: creating canary now, will post helm release id shortly :rocket:
deploy-bot: helm-release tiny-pod-canary v2.3.1 deployed by olivia at 6195551245
maya: canary looks good on one node, no evictions in the next 2m. if stable, roll to 10% then 100%
sam: i'll leave the rollback PR draft but hold merge unless canary fails
jordan: cost delta so far ~3.6% in ap-south1 for last 30m, likely an hour spike. I'll monitor and escalate if crosses 5%
maya: thanks all. lesson: node-label rollouts must include a compatibility checklist for tolerations + topology constraints. let's add that to the rollout template
noah: agreed — filing a small RFC for rollout preflight checks (labels/taints/tolerations/topology) after this
olivia: ack, will follow up with PR for checklist
maya: closing thread when canary is at 100% or rollback happens. :thumbsup:
